correctness.rationale: A triple using three distinct support lines is independent by leaf elimination on the three-edge tree in K₂,₂; a triple using two points on a support line and one off it is independent as well. Thus the only three-point lines are the four support lines. A plane with linear coefficients x_i contains an exponent a on ij iff x_i=ζ^a x_j. If it contains a support line, the two associated coefficients vanish. Then either a third coefficient vanishes, giving a coordinate-face plane with two adjacent support lines, or the two opposite coefficients are nonzero and can contribute at most one point on the opposite line. If there is no whole support line, three contained points on three distinct sides force nonzero coefficients and the balanced fourth exponent by the cycle equation. This establishes the plane classification and why a balanced quadruple is spanned by any three members. Independently reproduced all 4096 subsets by constructing distinct spans via canonical RREF over Q(ζ), rather than using the supplied incidence formulas or determinant checker. The exact negative masks are 63, 455, 3640, 4032, 4095. Opposite support lines span the four-dimensional ambient vector space, so the full negative configuration has rank four; the other four are adjacent whole support-line pairs, each of rank three. The profiles are exactly (12,58,43,−1) and (6,11,1,−2), and the independently logged profile for all twelve single deletions is (11,49,42,6).

value.rationale: A natural way to investigate a counterexample to the refined Purdy inequality is to ask if its failure is inherited by a smaller essential arrangement. The exact answer here is no, even under arbitrary multiple deletion; all proper negative subsets are classified and excluded by essentiality. This isolates a minimal failure within the historical example and avoids mistaking the four small planar negatives for smaller rank-four counterexamples. The natural inclusion classification is more useful than rediscovering the known full defect or checking a single deletion in isolation.
residual_risks: No global minimality, other μ_m restriction family, or universal deletion theorem is claimed.
